sections.html:
Gladstone is a third-class city with a council-manager government. Residents voted in November 1952 to incorporate rather than be annexed by Kansas City. Five council members are elected every three years on staggered terms, and a city manager runs daily operations.

The city covers 8.08 square miles, roughly from NE 55th and Englewood Road on the south to NE 77th on the north, with a panhandle reaching down to NW 44th Street. Missouri Routes 1 and 283 link it to North Kansas City and Kansas City, U.S. 169 sits less than 1.5 miles off the western border, and I-29 passes near the southern tip. North Oak Trafficway carries much of the shopping. Four small enclaves (Oakview, Oakwood Park, Oakwood and Oaks) sit in the southwest corner, so check the address you are selling falls inside Gladstone before you call the city.

The median owner-occupied home value is $231,500, and the town skews settled: 91.6% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Population was estimated at 27,497 in July 2025.

sections.h2: City forms and brochures before a sale
sections.html:
The Community Development Department publishes the permit applications and plain-language brochures most useful before a sale. Its phone number is (816) 423-4111. Payments cannot be made online, so you pay by mail or in person.

The permit list covers building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, dumpster, portable storage container and sump pump permits. It also includes an Abandoned or Vacant Property Registration Application, an Apartment Buildings Registration Application and a Residential Sale Permit Application. Call the department and ask whether your kind of sale needs that last one. The brochure library includes Planning a Residential Sale, Property Maintenance and Nuisance Guidelines, Home Repair Resources and Beware of Foreclosure Rescue Scams.

  • Ask whether open or expired permits on the house must be closed before you sign a contract.
  • Read the nuisance guidelines and fix any exterior issue the city would cite.
  • If you stopped living in the house, ask about the vacant property registration.
  • Read the foreclosure scam brochure if a stranger offers to rescue a house that is behind on payments.

sections.h2: Clay County taxes, prepayments and recording
sections.html:
Gladstone sits in Clay County. The county collector bills your real estate tax, and the county Recorder of Deeds files your deed. Bills normally go out by mid-November. Missouri statutes require payment by December 31 whether or not a bill arrived, and anyone without one by November 30 should call 816-407-3200.

A payment postmarked after December 31 draws a one-time 9% penalty plus interest of 1.5% per month on the unpaid balance. External drop boxes stay open around the clock, and deposits before midnight on December 31 count as on time. Online bill pay often reaches the office without a postmark, so the county dates those payments by the date printed on the check.

Clay County lets owners prepay. You can send $25 or more between March 1 and September 30. The money is held until bills are generated, applied in late October, and earns no interest. If you sell after making a prepayment, tell the title company before closing so the money is sorted out at the table.

The Assessor revalues real property every two years on January 1 of odd-numbered years under RSMo 137.115. That value carries into the even year except for new construction and improvements. The Senior Real Estate Property Tax Relief Program takes sign-ups each year from January 1 to March 31, so older owners should watch for that window.

Before listing, check the county billing portal for your parcel and confirm the prior year is paid. For recording, call the Recorder of Deeds at 816-407-3550 or write recorder@claycountymo.gov and ask for the current fee schedule.

sections.h2: Gladstone schools and landmarks buyers ask about
sections.html:
The North Kansas City School District serves Gladstone. Elementary boundaries that reach into the city include Chapel Hill, Linden West, Meadowbrook and Oakwood Manor. Most of Gladstone is zoned to Antioch Middle School, which is inside the city. Most addresses feed Oak Park High School in Kansas City, while the portion south of NW Englewood Road feeds Northgate Middle School and North Kansas City High School. A branch of the Mid-Continent Public Library is in town.

Maple Woods Natural Area, a remnant of the mesic forest that once covered the site, is a National Natural Landmark inside the city.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Gladstone
sections.html:
Three paths cover most sales here. The right one depends on repair needs, timing and how much of the process you want to manage yourself.

  • An agent listing suits a house in good shape in a school zone buyers know. Expect showings, a buyer inspection and a financing timeline.
  • A direct cash purchase suits a house with deferred work, tenants, or an estate that needs a fast and quiet close. The buyer takes the house in its current condition, and there are no showings or repair negotiations.
  • A for-sale-by-owner approach suits a seller comfortable handling contracts, disclosures and city paperwork alone.

Selling to a cash buyer usually skips the listing photos, open houses, appraisal contingency and buyer repair requests. The trade is that you should compare more than one offer, since price and closing costs vary between buyers.

Compare each offer by what you take home after tax proration, any lien payoff, title charges and recording. Ask every buyer who pays closing costs, how long they need and whether the offer depends on a loan.

sections.h2: If the house is behind on payments
sections.html:
Call your lender first to learn your options. Read the city's Beware of Foreclosure Rescue Scams brochure before you sign anything with a stranger who offers to take over the loan. Speak with an attorney if you want legal advice on a deed or contract.

A sale before a foreclosure date can stop the process and leave you with whatever equity remains. Gather your latest mortgage statement, the tax bill and any permit paperwork so a buyer can give you a number quickly. At closing the title company pays off the loan and any liens, prorates the tax bill, and sends you the balance.

faqs.q: Does Gladstone make sellers get an inspection before closing?
faqs.a: Community Development lists a Residential Sale Permit Application and a Planning a Residential Sale brochure. Call (816) 423-4111 to learn which steps apply to your sale before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: Which county records a Gladstone deed?
faqs.a: Clay County. The Recorder of Deeds can be reached at 816-407-3550 or recorder@claycountymo.gov for the current fee schedule and document standards.

faqs.q: What happens if Clay County property tax is paid late?
faqs.a: A payment postmarked after December 31 carries a one-time 9% penalty plus 1.5% interest per month on the unpaid balance.

faqs.q: I prepaid my Clay County taxes and then sold the house. What now?
faqs.a: Tell your title company before closing. Prepayments are held in a separate account, applied to the annual bill in late October, and refunded only after billing files are complete.
Slowly. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 27,497, up 1.6% from the April 2020 base of 27,058.
